issues.legal_issue: A tribunal may correct an earlier acceptance of a land surrender, even after an inquiry, when the declarant offered land that had already been acquired and vested in the State.
material_facts: A declarant’s land-ceiling proceedings determined that land was surplus, and a surrender of land was accepted after an inquiry.
The land offered for surrender had already been acquired in separate proceedings and had vested in the State.
After the earlier acceptance, the tribunal verified the acquisition records and substituted alternative land as surplus; the appellate tribunal upheld that decision.
The High Court held that the tribunal could not change its decision after conducting an inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The tribunal was justified in modifying its earlier order because the surrender involved fraud; the High Court’s order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Fraud involves deception and injury, and a deliberate false representation or suppression of a material fact to secure an advantage can vitiate proceedings. In public law, fraud includes knowingly and deliberately disclosing incorrect facts to procure an exercise of power that otherwise would not have occurred; the misrepresentation must concern a condition relevant to that power. Fraud vitiates even solemn proceedings, and an earlier inquiry or order does not preserve an outcome obtained by fraud. The Court relied on Section 10(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973, in relation to the inquiry on surrender, and on Section 17 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, as a definition of fraud while distinguishing public-law fraud from private-law fraud. It also relied on Dr. Vimla v. Delhi Administration, Indian Bank v. Satyam Fibres (India) Pvt. Ltd., S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jagannath, Ram Chandra Singh v. Savitri Devi, Shrisht Dhawan v. M/s. Shaw Brothers, Derry v. Peek, Roshan Deen v. Preeti Lal, Ram Preeti Yadav v. U.P. Board of High School and Intermediate Education, Ashok Leyland Ltd. v. State of T.N., Gowrishankar v. Joshi Amba Shankar Family Trust, and Lazarus Estate Ltd. v. Beasley.

rule.if: land_ceiling_surrender_proceeding and prior_surrender_acceptance_after_inquiry and offered_land_already_acquired_and_vested and offered_land_presented_as_available_for_surrender

predicates.land_ceiling_surrender_proceeding: The matter concerns surrender of land in proceedings to determine whether a landholder exceeds a landholding ceiling.
predicates.prior_surrender_acceptance_after_inquiry: The tribunal accepted a proposed surrender after conducting an inquiry.
predicates.offered_land_already_acquired_and_vested: The land offered for surrender had already been acquired and had vested in the State.
predicates.offered_land_presented_as_available_for_: The declarant offered the already-acquired land as land available to surrender.

issues.definition: When a tribunal has accepted a surrender after an inquiry but the declarant offered as available land that had already been acquired and vested in the State, the tribunal may reopen and correct its prior order.
